Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 107, verses 1–7:

﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ It has been said that this was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. It has also been said that it is general in meaning, and that "al-din" (the Recompense) here means the religion (millah) or the reckoning (jaza'). ﴿For that is the one who repulses the orphan﴾, that is, pushes him away violently. This repulsion may be from feeding him and showing kindness to him, or from his wealth and rights, and the latter is more severe. One who does not urge the feeding of the needy will not feed him all the more. This sentence is the answer to "have you seen" (ara'ayta), because its meaning is "tell me," so it is like a question and an answer. The meaning is: look at the one who denies the religion, and you will find in him these ugly characteristics and evil deeds, and that is only because religion moves its adherent to do good deeds and to abandon evil ones. So the purpose of the speech is to censure the disbelievers and their conditions. ﴿So woe to those who pray﴾. It has been said that this was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the hypocrite, and according to this view half of the surah is Meccan and half is Medinan, as stated by Abu Zayd al-Suhayli. This is because the mention of Abu Jahl and other disbelievers occurs most often in the Meccan surahs, while the mention of heedlessness concerning the prayer and of showing off (riya') occurs there only as a description of those who were in Medina, especially according to the view that it was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. It has also been said that the whole surah is Meccan, and this is the most well-known view, and its last part, according to this view, was revealed concerning a man who embraced Islam in Mecca but whose faith was not sound. It has also been said that it is Medinan. Heedlessness concerning the prayer means abandoning it or delaying it out of negligence toward it.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about those who are heedless of their prayer, and he said: "Those who delay it beyond its time." 'Ata' ibn Yasar said: "Praise be to Allah, who said ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾ and did not say 'in their prayer.'" ﴿Those who show off﴾ is from riya', meaning their prayer is for the sake of people and not for Allah. ﴿And withhold common kindness﴾: this describes them with stinginess and with providing little benefit to people. Regarding al-ma'un (common kindness) there are four opinions. The first is that it is zakat. The second is that it is wealth in the dialect of Quraysh. The third is that it is water. The fourth is that it is what people lend to one another, such as utensils, the axe, the bucket, and the scissors. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "What is the thing whose withholding is not permitted?" He said: "Water, fire, and salt." And in some narrations he added: "The needle and the leaven."
